([[Bel Aire, Kansas]]) | college = * [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] (2017–2020) * [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] (2020–2021) | career_start = 2021 | draft_year = 2021 | years1 = 2021–2023 | team1 = [[Skyliners Frankfurt]] | years2 = 2023–2024 | team2 = [[Palencia Baloncesto|CD Zunder Palencia]] | years3 = 2024–present | team3 = [[Kagoshima Rebnise]] | highlights = * Second-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] (2021) * WCC Defensive Player of the Year (2021) }} '''Matt Haarms''' (born 22 April 1997) is a Dutch professional [[basketball]] player for [[Kagoshima Rebnise]] of the [[B.League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue Boilermakers]] and the [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU Cougars]]. Haarms also plays for the [[Netherlands men's national basketball team]]. ==Early life== Haarms is the son of Martine van Hoorn and Peter Haarms. He was born and grew up in Amsterdam. He initially played soccer and judo before taking up basketball. Haarms purchased an outdoor hoop at the age of 14 so he could practice more.{{cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2018-09-17/college-basketball-how-7-footer-matt-haarms-made-it-purdue|title=College basketball: How 7-footer Matt Haarms made it to Purdue after an Amsterdam childhood|first=Andy|last=Katz|website=NCAA.com|date=September 18, 2018|accessdate=January 10, 2020}} Haarms joined a club team, the Harlemlakers, and admittedly was very poor at first but soon developed into one of the top talents in the country. Haarms then moved to Spain and played for [[Joventut Badalona]]'s junior team. He helped the team reach the championship game of the tournament and hit 5-of-7 three-point shots in the semifinal against Real Madrid. He was offered a professional contract in Spain but declined the invitation. Instead, Haarms moved to the United States to complete a [[postgraduate year]] at Sunrise Christian Academy in [[Bel Aire, Kansas]].{{cite web|last=Baird|first=Nathan|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2018/01/19/bambi-pistol-pete-purdue-star-matt-haarms-improbable-basketball-journey/1035115001/|title=Matt Haarms' improbable journey to Purdue|work=[[Journal & Courier]]|date=March 16, 2018|accessdate=January 10, 2020}} He started to receive collegiate attention when he joined the Chauncey Billups AAU Elite team. Haarms committed to playing college basketball for [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] over offers from [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] and [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]], becoming the Boilermakers' sixth international player since 1952. He chose Purdue because he liked coach [[Matt Painter]] and the program's record of developing [[Forward-center|big men]].{{cite news |last1=Baird |first1=Nathan |title=Matt Haarms commits to Purdue basketball |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2016/10/05/purdue-basketball-matt-haarms-commitment/91638610/ |accessdate=January 10, 2020 |work=[[Journal & Courier]] |date=October 5, 2016}} ==College career== ===Purdue=== Haarms enrolled at Purdue a semester early and [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] the second half of the 2016–17 season because the NCAA ruled he would have lost a season of eligibility had he stayed at Sunrise Christian.{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2016/12/15/purdue-2017-signee-enroll-early/95482978/|title=Purdue 2017 signee will enroll early|work=[[Journal & Courier]]|date=December 15, 2016|accessdate=January 10, 2020}} As a redshirt freshman he averaged 4.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game in 37 games.{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2018/10/30/purdues-matt-haarms-wants-his-new-style-extend-big-man-tradition/1687421002/|title=Purdue's Matt Haarms wants his new style to extend big man tradition|work=[[Journal & Courier]]|date=October 30, 2018|accessdate=January 10, 2020}} His 79 blocked shots were the second-most by a Purdue freshman. Haarms started against [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] and [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]] in the NCAA Tournament after [[Isaac Haas]] injured his elbow and had a combined 11 points and nine rebounds in the two games. He averaged 9.4 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 2.1 blocks per game as a redshirt sophomore.{{cite web|url=https://www.hammerandrails.com/2019/10/5/20900719/purdue-basketball-matt-haarms-preview|title=32 Days to Purdue Basketball: Matt Haarms|first=Travis|last=Miller|website=HammerAndRails.com|date=October 5, 2019|accessdate=January 10, 2020}} On 19 February 2019 Haarms hit a last-second shot to defeat [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] after being taunted by Indiana fans all game.{{cite news |last1=Doyel |first1=Gregg |title=Doyel: Hair-flipping, fist-pumping, shot-blocking Matt Haarms is Purdue's thermometer |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/columnists/gregg-doyel/2019/03/27/purdue-basketball-center-matt-haarms-keying-march-madness-2019-run/3286767002/ |accessdate=January 10, 2020 |work=[[Indianapolis Star]] |date=March 28, 2019}} Haarms suffered a head injury in a loss to [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] on 15 December, and missed the following game against [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball|Ohio]].{{cite news |last1=Dopirak |first1=Dustin |title=Purdue can function without Matt Haarms, but it’s going to require some alterations |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1469788/2019/12/18/purdue-can-function-without-matt-haarms-but-its-going-to-require-some-alterations/ |access-date=January 10, 2020 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=December 18, 2019}} On 2 January 2020 Haarms scored a career-high 26 points on 11-of-16 shooting in a double-overtime win against [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]].{{cite news |title=Haarms scores 26 points, Purdue beats Minnesota 83-78 2OT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166146 |accessdate=January 10, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 2, 2020}} He became the second player in Big Ten history, and first since 2007, to lead the league in field goal percentage and blocked shots in the same season. He suffered a hip injury in a double-overtime loss to [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] on 9 January.{{cite web|url=https://www.hammerandrails.com/2020/1/9/21059354/purdue-78-michigan-84-double-overtime-again|title=Purdue 78, Michigan 84 - Double-Overtime (Again)|first=Casey|last=Bartley|website=HammerAndRails.com|date=January 9, 2020|accessdate=January 10, 2020}} As a junior, Haarms averaged 8.6 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 2 blocks per game.{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Travis |title=2020-21 Purdue Basketball Homework: Matt Haarms |url=https://www.hammerandrails.com/2020/3/15/21181102/2020-21-purdue-basketball-matt-haarms-outlook |website=Hammer and Rails |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=April 3, 2020 |date=March 15, 2020}} Following the season, he transferred from Purdue.{{cite news |last1=Carmin |first1=Mike |title=Purdue basketball's Matt Haarms enters transfer portal |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/2020/04/06/purdue-basketballs-matt-haarms-enters-transfer-portal/2955615001/ |accessdate=April 6, 2020 |work=[[Lafayette Journal & Courier]] |date=April 6, 2020}} After his last season at Purdue, he was named to the 2021 Kareem Abdul-Jabbar award watch list. ===BYU=== On 23 April 2020 Haarms announced that he would transfer to [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] over offers from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]], gaining immediate eligibility as a graduate transfer.{{cite web |last1=Gonzalez |first1=Norma |title=BYU lands Purdue center Matt Haarms, the biggest name in college basketball’s transfer portal |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/byu-cougars/2020/04/23/byu-lands-purdue-center/ |website=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]] |accessdate=April 23, 2020 |date=April 23, 2020}} He averaged 11.3 points, 5 rebounds, and 2 blocks per game. Haarms was named the [[West Coast Conference]] Defensive Player of the Year and was selected to the All-WCC second team. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing the additional season of eligibility the NCAA granted due to the COVID-19 pandemic.{{cite news |last1=Judd |first1=Brandon |title=Matt Haarms officially says he won’t return to BYU: ‘It’s time to move on into the next chapter of my life’ |url=https://www.deseret.com/2021/5/7/22425198/matt-haarms-officially-says-he-wont-return-to-byu-basketball-center-mark-pope |access-date=June 22, 2021 |work=[[Deseret News]] |date=May 7, 2021}} ==Professional career== On 13 July 2021, Haarms signed his first professional contract with German club [[Skyliners Frankfurt]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]]. He signed a two-year contract.{{cite news |title=2,21 METER PURE BASKETBALLLEIDENSCHAFT – FRAPORT SKYLINERS VERPFLICHTEN MATT HAARMS |url=https://www.fraport-skyliners.de/news-service/details/221-meter-pure-basketballleidenschaft-fraport-skyliners-verpflichten-matt-haarms/ |lang=de|access-date=14 July 2021 |work=Fraport Skyliners |date=13 July 2021}} On 20 June 2024 Haarms signed with [[Kagoshima Rebnise]] of the [[B.League]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.rebnise.jp/news/detail/id=15813|title=【新規】Matt Haarms選手 2024-25シーズン 選手契約締結のお知らせ|language=Japanese|publisher=Kagoshima Rebnise|date=June 20, 2024|access-date=Aug 19, 2024}} ==National team career== Haarms competed for the [[Netherlands national under-19 basketball team|Netherlands under-19 team]] at the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship Division B]] in [[Austria]] and averaged 4.5 points and 3.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Matt Haarms |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/lid_38135_cp/1/pid/115114/q/Matt/rpp/100/_//players.html |website=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=January 10, 2020}}{{dead link|date=April 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Haarms was selected for the [[Netherlands national basketball team|Netherlands senior team]] for the first time in November 2021.{{cite news |title=Matt Haarms kan 'eindelijk' uitkomen voor Nederland |url=https://www.basketball.nl/nieuwsoverzicht/matt-haarms-kan-eindelijk-uitkomen-voor-nederland/ |access-date=28 November 2021 |work=Basketball.nl |language=nl}} On 26 November 2021 Haarms made his debut in a loss against [[Iceland men's national basketball team|Iceland]].{{cite web |title=Basketbalmannen beginnen WK-kwalificatie met nipte nederlaag tegen IJsland |url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2407216-basketbalmannen-beginnen-wk-kwalificatie-met-nipte-nederlaag-tegen-ijsland |website=nos.nl |access-date=28 November 2021 |language=nl}} He played at [[EuroBasket 2022]], coming off the bench and averaging 3.3 points and 3.8 rebounds as a back-up center.{{Cite web |title=Matt HAARMS at the FIBA EuroBasket 2022 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/player/Matt-Haarms |access-date=2022-09-16 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College===
